clue.text: Wine transporter?

parts.note: reads as a lorry or tanker carrying wine, but means a classic automobile described by its year of production, the way a good wine is

explanation.definitionFit: A car from an old, celebrated year of manufacture is described with the wine-maker's word for a year's produce.

clue.text: Six does change records

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of the word does

explanation.surface: Six female deer alter their records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like the verb or female deer; it is the anagram fodder that 'change' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded films on tape or disc are recordings, so records in the noun sense.

clue.text: Detail in French resort on Tuscany's borders

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

indicators.note: the borders of Tuscany's are its first and last letters, ignoring the possessive

explanation.surface: Something detailed about a French resort next to the edges of Tuscany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' takes the first and last letters of Tuscany, T and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine point or subtle distinction is a small detail.

clue.text: The price of a confession?

parts.note: a confession is an act of owning up, so the cost of owning up is read as the charge for getting in

explanation.definitionFit: An entry charge is paid for being let in, and owning up is also called making this.

clue.text: A Greek idol enveloped in generosity

indicators.note: the letters sit wrapped up inside the single word generosity

explanation.surface: A Greek god wrapped in a spirit of giving.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love was worshipped as a deity, an idol in the clue's sense.

clue.text: Mature support for 18-30 group for instance

parts.note: to mature is to grow older, to age
a bracket is a support fixed to a wall for a shelf

explanation.surface: Mature backing for an 18-30 holiday crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: People aged eighteen to thirty form a band of years, an example of a range classified by years.

clue.text: Measure that's too expensive to lose heart

indicators.note: losing its heart means a word drops one of its central letters

parts.note: a steep price is one too high

explanation.surface: A measure that costs too much to stay keen about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose heart' removes one of the middle Es of STEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a measure taken, an action towards a goal.

clue.text: An occasion for drink with some in Boston?

definitions.text: An occasion for drink with some in Boston?

parts.words: An occasion for drink with some in Boston?
parts.note: an afternoon gathering over cups, which also recalls the 1773 protest when colonists dumped chests of leaves into Boston harbour

explanation.definitionFit: A social gathering for afternoon cups, and the name of the famous Boston protest of 1773.

clue.text: Fencing friend is saying "help"

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: saying signals that a word is spoken and we write what we hear

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A fencer's friend calls out for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saying' turns AID into its sound-alike ADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of stakes, so fencing as a material or barrier.

clue.text: Most organic matter, in fact, has broken down

definitions.text: Most organic matter, in fact, has broken down

parts.words: Most organic matter, in fact, has broken down
parts.note: the sentence reads as a fact about rotting, describing material that has rotted away

explanation.definitionFit: Rotted organic matter is said to have broken down into simpler parts.

clue.text: Loudly lobby — in drag!

indicators.note: loudly signals a word spoken aloud and written as heard

parts.note: a hall is an entrance lobby

explanation.surface: A loud lobbying effort by someone in drag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loudly' turns HALL into the sound-alike HAUL; 'drag' is the verb, to pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul something is to pull or drag it along.

clue.text: At once honest and distant

parts.note: straight means honest or upright
away means distant or absent

explanation.surface: Someone at once honest and aloof.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediately, without any delay.

clue.text: It's over 90 degrees and dull

definitions.meaning: an angle greater than a right angle

explanation.definitionFit: An angle wider than a right angle, and a blunt or slow-witted person.

clue.text: Few stars can be worried about what carpenters might use

indicators.note: worried suggests the letters of few stars being shaken into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fretful stars worrying about carpentry tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine-bladed saws for cutting curves in wood are tools a woodworker might use.

clue.text: Being poor, Stephen Ryan has no time for this investment

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of the names are badly arranged and need reworking
having no time means the letter for time is dropped

explanation.surface: A hard-up man named Stephen Ryan can't spare a moment for this investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no time' removes T from STEPHENRYAN, leaving SEPHENRYAN; 'Being poor' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A share of very low price is a kind of stock-market investment.

clue.text: Fascinated by detective inspector's feeling let down

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector; the 's adds S
enchanted means fascinated

explanation.surface: A detective inspector's charm has worn off.
explanation.definitionFit: Disillusioned and disappointed after an earlier enthusiasm.

clue.text: Stays away from upper classes with stigmas

parts.note: A and B are the top social grades in British market research
stains are marks of disgrace, stigmas

explanation.surface: The upper classes keep clear of anything shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: British social grading runs A, B, C1, C2, D, E, so A and B are the upper classes.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from something, especially drink or voting, is to keep off it.

clue.text: "Sunday went slowly" was written without care

parts.note: crawled means moved slowly

explanation.surface: A lazy Sunday dragged on, written up sloppily.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastily or messily penned, as of handwriting.

clue.text: Gasbag conned cooked food in the morning

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of gasbag conned are worked into a new dish

explanation.surface: A windbag fooled into making breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British cooked breakfast of fried rashers and eggs.

clue.text: Doctor got up feeling sullen

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
rose means got up

explanation.surface: A doctor got out of bed feeling grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy and bad-tempered, a synonym of sullen.

clue.text: Put outside private group of musicians

indicators.note: outside signals one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: to set is to put
Pte is the abbreviation for the army rank of private

explanation.surface: A private group of musicians kept away from others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' here is the verb in its past sense, set; the army abbreviation for private sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven musicians playing together form an ensemble.

clue.text: Cross, being reluctant to follow empty tractor

indicators.note: follow places the second piece after the first
an empty word keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: averse means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: Reluctant to trail behind an empty tractor on a crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for angry, but it is the verb meaning go across.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across.

clue.text: Enter right into Midlands town, at a crawl for example

indicators.note: into signals one piece put inside another

parts.note: Stoke-on-Trent, known as Stoke, is a city in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: Enter the right way into a Midlands town, crawling slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: STOKE is Stoke-on-Trent, a pottery city in central England; 'into' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The crawl is one swimming style, an example of a swimming technique.

clue.text: Using speech is ethical if beginning mass

indicators.note: the word for mass would stand at the start, so taking it away from the front leaves the answer

parts.note: moral means ethical
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Speaking out is ethical when starting Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the answer is the ethical word if begun with M; removing that M from MORAL leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written, done by mouth.

clue.text: Beheading puts an end to troubles

indicators.note: beheading takes off the first letter of a word

parts.note: kills means puts an end to

explanation.surface: A beheading certainly ends one's troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Misfortunes and problems are troubles.

clue.text: Vessel found in Arab town or re-settlement

indicators.note: re-settlement suggests the letters of Arab town or being settled again in a new order

explanation.surface: A ship located in an Arab town or a resettled community.
explanation.definitionFit: A long thin canal boat is a type of vessel.

clue.text: Team talk of having expressed regret

indicators.note: talk of signals a word spoken aloud and written as heard

parts.note: sighed means expressed regret with a breath

explanation.surface: A team's chatter about having regrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talk of' turns SIGHED into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a sports team.

clue.text: Disposition of the lower classes — trick people with time

parts.note: D and E are the lowest social grades in British market research
a ploy is a trick
men means people

explanation.surface: The attitude of the working classes is to trick people given time.
explanation.walkthrough: British social grading runs A, B, C1, C2, D, E, so D and E are the lower classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Disposition in the military sense is the arrangement of troops, their positioning.
